The intent of the fellowship is to focus on high risk research: ambitious projects that may not produce results, but will have lasting impact if they work.

Our focus is on frontier research: order-of-magnitude improvements, rather than disposable papers barely better than baseline.
The goal of these fellowships is to give awardees uninterrupted time to focus on harder open problems, with adequate compute, talented peers, and weekly 1:1 mentorship from senior researchers but without chasing specific metrics.

Location: you may reside anywhere in the world, excluding sanctioned jurisdictions. This will be a remote fellowship. We do not sponsor visas.

title: Engineering Manager
description:
About the role
Gcore operates a global edge platform: a content delivery network, authoritative and recursive DNS, and the traffic management layer that decides where requests land. It carries production traffic for media, gaming and enterprise customers, and the difference between a good and a bad engineering decision is visible in latency and availability within minutes.
We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the teams that build and run the CDN control plane, the edge request path, the analytics and logging pipeline, and our traffic management services.
This is a leadership role with real technical weight. You will not be writing production code day to day, but you will be expected to hold your own in an architecture discussion, question a proposed fix when the evidence is thin, and own the consequences when something breaks at 3am.
What You Will Do

• Lead four engineering teams covering the control plane, the core edge and proxy layer, the analytics and logging platform, and DNS and traffic management.

• Own delivery on a two-week cadence: planning, commitments, and honest reporting on what shipped and what did not.

• Set and defend technical priorities with Product, Support and Maintenance. A large part of the job is deciding what the teams will not do this quarter.

• Own the incident and post-incident process for your area: severity calls, root-cause analysis, and making sure prevention work actually gets built rather than filed and forgotten.

• Run the on-call rotation for your teams and keep the escalation path clear.

• Develop your engineers and tech leads through regular one-to-ones, feedback and growth planning, and hire well when you have headcount.

• Improve how the department works: planning, prioritisation, quality standards, documentation, and service ownership.

• Ensure AI tools and approaches are being adopted.

The kind of problems you will be closer to
A sense of the work rather than an exhaustive list:

• Cache and shielding behaviour: how a large origin is protected, and how configuration changes propagate to the edge safely.

• Config delivery at scale: pushing configuration to a global fleet quickly, and knowing where its limits are.

• Analytics cost and performance: keeping a high-volume ClickHouse estate fast and affordable.

• Traffic steering and failover.

• Observability that catches customer impact before the customer does.

What We are Looking For

• Four or more years leading software engineering teams, including experience managing tech leads.

• Production experience with internet infrastructure: CDN, DNS, reverse proxies, or large-scale distributed systems.

• Enough depth to reason independently about HTTP caching, nginx behaviour, TLS and SNI, and anycast routing.

• A track record of owning incident response and post-incident follow-through, not just attending the calls.

• Comfort running several teams at once, and the confidence to say no to a stakeholder with a clear reason.

• Experience with distributed teams spanning European and Asian working hours.

Nice to Have

• C, Rust, Go, Python, at a level where you can review a change.

• Prometheus, Grafana, ClickHouse and distributed tracing.

• Kubernetes alongside bare-metal fleet operations.

• Experience at a CDN, DNS or cloud provider, or at a network operator.

• Experience acting as product owner for platform work.

What We can be Straight with You About
This is a mature platform with real customers and real legacy. Some services are owned by a single engineer, and reducing that dependency is part of the job. Product ownership for platform work is currently shared between engineering and product management, which means backlog quality depends partly on you. We would rather you knew that before joining than discovered it in month two.
In return you get a genuinely interesting technical domain, a small enough organisation that your decisions are visible, and direct access to the people setting product direction.

The Principal Business Intelligence and Automation Lead owns the business-facing capability that turns operational data into trusted, actionable decisions across HealthEdge . This is an enterprise capability, not a reporting function: the role sets the agenda for what gets measured, what gets automated, and how the business and Technology work together to deliver it.
The person in this role operates as a strategic partner to Operations, Product, and Technology leadership - translating business priorities into data and automation requirements, and shaping HealthEdge 's data strategy from the operational vantage point. The role does not own the underlying data platform, architecture, or engineering; that ownership sits with the Data & Analytics Platform team in Technology. The Principal Business Intelligence and Automation Lead owns the demand side of the equation: priorities, requirements, and business outcomes.
Key Responsibilities:

• Set enterprise priorities for operational reporting and dashboards, ensuring the business consistently has trusted, decision-ready information.

• Lead business intelligence and analytics efforts that surface insight - not just data - for Operations, Product, and executive stakeholders.

• Identify and drive business process automation opportunities, including applying AI where it measurably improves speed, accuracy, or cost.

• Translate business needs into clear data and technology requirements that the Platform team and other Technology partners can build against.

• Influence HealthEdge 's long-term data strategy by bringing operational priorities and real-world business context into platform and architecture planning.

• Act as the primary business-side partner to the Data & Analytics Platform team, Product, and Technology - owning requirements definition, prioritization, and business validation of delivered solutions.

• Build and maintain a prioritized roadmap of reporting, analytics, and automation initiatives based on operational impact.

• Represent the voice of the business in Technology governance and planning forums where data and automation investment decisions are made.
Ownership & Partnership Boundaries:
This capability is deliberately split to keep accountability clear as it scales:

• Principal Business Intelligence and Automation Lead owns: reporting and automation priorities, business requirements, opportunity identification, business-side data strategy input, and partnership with Product and Technology to validate that delivered solutions meet business needs.

• Data & Analytics Platform team (Technology) owns: the underlying data platform, architecture, engineering, and technical roadmap.
Neither side substitutes for the other. The Platform team is not accountable for deciding what the business should measure or automate next; the Principal Business Intelligence and Automation Lead is not accountable for how the platform is engineered.
